To find the proportionality factor $C$, we express the quantum state in the polar (Madelung) representation:
$$\psi(x) = \sqrt{\mathcal{P}(x)}\, e^{i S(x)/\hbar}$$

Differentiating with respect to the parameters yields:
$$\frac{\partial_\mu \psi}{\psi} = \frac{\partial_\mu \sqrt{\mathcal{P}}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{P}}} + \frac{i}{\hbar} \partial_\mu S$$

The Madelung--Bohm current velocity $\pi_\mu$ and osmotic velocity $u_\mu$ are defined as:
$$\pi_\mu = \frac{1}{m} \partial_\mu S \implies \partial_\mu S = m \pi_\mu$$
$$u_\mu = \frac{\hbar}{2m} \frac{\partial_\mu \mathcal{P}}{\mathcal{P}} = \frac{\hbar}{m} \frac{\partial_\mu \sqrt{\mathcal{P}}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{P}}} \implies \frac{\partial_\mu \sqrt{\mathcal{P}}}{\sqrt{\mathcal{P}}} = \frac{m}{\hbar} u_\mu$$

Substituting these into the logarithmic derivative of the wave function:
$$\frac{\partial_\mu \psi}{\psi} = \frac{m}{\hbar} u_\mu + \frac{i m}{\hbar} \pi_\mu = \frac{i m}{\hbar} (\pi_\mu - i u_\mu) = \frac{i m}{\hbar} \eta_\mu$$
where $\eta_\mu = \pi_\mu - i u_\mu$ is the complex velocity field.

The Fubini--Study metric $g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}}$ on the projective Hilbert space corresponds to the real part of the quantum geometric tensor:
$$g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \operatorname{Re}\bigl[ \langle \partial_\mu \psi | \partial_\nu \psi \rangle - \langle \partial_\mu \psi | \psi \rangle \langle \psi | \partial_\nu \psi \rangle \bigr]$$

Expressing this in terms of the complex velocity field $\eta_\mu$:
$$\langle \partial_\mu \psi | \partial_\nu \psi \rangle - \langle \partial_\mu \psi | \psi \rangle \langle \psi | \partial_\nu \psi \rangle = \frac{m^2}{\hbar^2} \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_\mu^*, \eta_\nu)_{\mathcal{P}}$$

Taking the real part:
$$\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Cov}(\eta_\mu^*, \eta_\nu)_{\mathcal{P}} = \operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu, \pi_\nu)_{\mathcal{P}} + \operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu, u_\nu)_{\mathcal{P}}$$

Thus, the metric takes the form:
$$g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = \frac{m^2}{\hbar^2} \bigl[ \operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu, \pi_\nu) + \operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu, u_\nu) \bigr]_{\mathcal{P}}$$

Substituting $x = \hbar$, the proportionality factor is:
$$C = \frac{m^2}{x^2}$$

ANSWER: m^2/x^2
